reasons.A: Opens with a rhetorical question and keeps the passage's long, semicolon-joined sentences, first-person hedging and mid-paragraph questions; a slight pile-up of hedges at the close, but the movement and stance match best.
reasons.B: Measured, formal, uncontracted and balanced in the same register, but it has no questions and no first-person 'I', uses a dash the author avoids, and reads more like detached exposition than the author's reflective voice.
reasons.C: Short, clipped sentences, verbless fragments, casual modern diction ('happy path', 'sprint') and an assertive, prescriptive close; the rhythm and stance are far from the author's long hedged periods.
